name: vllm-project/humming
title: Independent RTX 5090 test of vLLM's Humming kernels: 4-bit Qwen3.8-27B goes from 56.9 to 71.6 tok/s, about even with Marlin
summary: An outside test of the Humming quantized-kernel library (released by vLLM and Ant Group on Oct 21) on a consumer RTX 5090: with NVFP4 Qwen3.8-27B in vLLM, switching to Humming took a single request from 56.9 to 71.6 tokens/s, 26% over the kernel vLLM picks by default on that card. Against the older Marlin 4-bit kernel it was a tie (75.8 vs 77.1 tok/s), so the gain on this card is mainly over vLLM'

appearances.title: vLLM and Ant Group open-source Humming, one quantized GEMM kernel library across formats and GPUs
appearances.summary: vLLM and Ant Group released Humming, a JIT-compiled kernel library for quantized inference that covers many weight formats and GPU generations, including consumer SM120 cards. They report up to 5x kernel speedups and 14 to 43% higher end-to-end MoE throughput, so quantized models can run closer to their theoretical speed without a separate kernel per format.
